source: Cover and Hart (1967) Nearest neighbor pattern classification
finding: Founding result for nearest-case retrieval. With unlimited stored cases, the 1-nearest-neighbour rule makes at most about twice the error of the best possible (Bayes) classifier. The single nearest neighbour is admissible among k-NN rules.
numbers: Bounds: R* <= R <= 2R*(1-R*) for two classes; for M classes R* <= R <= R*(2 - M R*/(M-1)). R* = Bayes error, R = NN error. Holds for any metric in the limit of infinite sample.
quote: the probability of error of the nearest neighbor rule is bounded above by twice the Bayes probability of error
limits: Asymptotic only. Says nothing about small case bases, noisy or irrelevant features, or which metric is right.
agent_relevance: A case library can approach optimal accuracy with no model, but only with a meaningful distance and a large library. Our small class record is far from this limit.

source: Aha, Kibler and Albert (1991) Instance-based learning algorithms
finding: Defines IB1 (store everything, predict by nearest stored instance), IB2 (store only misclassified instances) and IB3 (keep a running accuracy record per instance and drop poor or noisy ones). Proves IB1 converges for a large class of concepts.
limits: Small UCI-era databases. IB1 to IB3 degrade fast with irrelevant attributes: storage grows and learning rate falls exponentially with dimension.
agent_relevance: A case library needs a retention filter. Keeping everything or only failures lets noise in. Keeping cases with a good retrieval record gave about 90% storage savings with equal or better accuracy.

source: Aha, Kibler and Albert (1991) IB2 noise failure and IB3 repair
finding: Storage reduction by 'keep what you got wrong' backfires under noise, because a noisy case is misclassified and so gets stored, then misleads later queries. IB3 fixes this with a significance test on each case's record.
numbers: Simple artificial domain at 10% noise: IB2 kept 76 instances, 20 of them noisy (26.3%); IB3 kept 25 and 0 noisy. Over 50 trials IB2 saved on average 28.3% noisy instances at that noise level. In one noisy run IB3 used only 5.8% of training instances to classify.
limits: Artificial domain. IB3 is slightly worse at 0% noise because it wrongly discards some true exceptions.
agent_relevance: Hard cases and noisy cases look the same at write time. Retain on measured later usefulness, not on first failure.

source: Aha, Kibler and Albert (1991) sparse classes (Primary Tumor)
finding: With many classes and few instances per class, nearest-case storage savings vanish. Primary Tumor has 11 concepts with under 10 instances each.
numbers: Primary Tumor accuracy (storage): IB1 34.7 (100), IB2 32.9 (71.3), IB3 38.6 (16.4), C4 37.8.
limits: Single medical dataset.
agent_relevance: Our class record is small and sparse per class. Expect weak retrieval unless cases are shared across classes by abstraction.

source: Ontanon (2020) An overview of distance and similarity functions for structured data
finding: Survey of similarity measures used by CBR, instance-based learning and kernels. Groups them by representation: feature vectors (Minkowski, cosine, Mahalanobis), sets (Jaccard, Tversky), sequences (edit distance), trees and graphs.
numbers: Tversky index: |X and Y| / (|X and Y| + alpha|X-Y| + beta|Y-X|). Jaccard is the special case alpha = beta = 1 (as printed in the text). Cosine differs from Minkowski by ignoring vector length.
limits: Survey, no new experiments. Notes much structured-data work uses ad-hoc functions chosen per application.
agent_relevance: Gives the menu for case similarity: sets of operator tags, sequences of steps, trees of subgoals. Pick by held-out same-class vs different-class retrieval tests.

source: Tversky (1977) Features of similarity
finding: Contrast model: similarity is a weighted match of shared features minus weighted distinctive features of each item, so it can be asymmetric and break the triangle inequality. Challenged the geometric (metric) view. Formula seen only through Ontanon (2020).
numbers: Not opened. Human judgement data from memory: asymmetry such as judging North Korea more like China than China like North Korea.
limits: Marked [M]. Human judgement data, not retrieval accuracy. Metric-space retrieval cannot reproduce asymmetry.
agent_relevance: Case similarity need not be symmetric: 'this case covers my problem' differs from 'my problem covers this case'.

source: Aamodt and Plaza (1994) Case-based reasoning: foundational issues, methodological variations, and system approaches
finding: Standard four-step CBR cycle: Retrieve, Reuse, Revise, Retain. Retrieval is split into identify features, initial match, select. Used as the base frame by CBR-KBQA and Memento, both read this session.
numbers: Not opened (PDF hosts failed). Cycle confirmed as cited in arXiv 2104.08762 and 2508.16153.
limits: Marked [M]. Written before dense embeddings.
agent_relevance: The 4R cycle is the template for our memory: library of solved subgoals, offer by similarity, keep by rule.

source: Richter (1995) The knowledge contained in similarity measures; Richter and Weber (2013) Case-Based Reasoning: A Textbook
finding: Knowledge containers view: a CBR system holds knowledge in four places (vocabulary, similarity measure, case base, adaptation knowledge) and knowledge can move between them. The similarity measure is itself a container of domain knowledge.
numbers: Not opened. Conceptual framework, no numbers.
limits: Marked [M]. Framework, not a tested claim.
agent_relevance: Design lever: a better similarity function and more cases are partial substitutes. We can measure which one the gains come from.

source: Bergmann (2001) / Richter and Weber (2013) local-global similarity
finding: Standard CBR similarity model: global similarity is a weighted aggregate of per-attribute local similarities. Feature weights carry the relevance knowledge.
numbers: Not opened. No numbers.
limits: Marked [M]. Assumes attribute-value cases; weights are set by experts or learned.
agent_relevance: A transparent, code-checkable retrieval score (G5: code selects) as an alternative to an opaque embedding cosine.

source: Smyth and Keane (1998) Adaptation-guided retrieval: questioning the similarity assumption in reasoning
finding: Argues the most similar case is not the most useful case. Retrieve by how cheap the case is to adapt, not by surface similarity. Page fetch returned only an HTML shell, so details are from memory.
numbers: Not opened. Numbers not recorded.
limits: Marked [M]. Original domain was control-software design; no LLM.
agent_relevance: The same finding reappears for LLMs in EPR and UDR: surface similarity is a weak proxy for usefulness.

source: Lenz and Burkhard (1996) Case retrieval nets
finding: Memory-network model of retrieval: information entities are nodes, activation spreads from query features through similarity arcs to cases. Gives fast retrieval and incremental case addition.
numbers: Not opened. No numbers.
limits: Marked [M].
agent_relevance: One way to index a growing library without a full scan.

source: Gentner and Forbus (1991) MAC/FAC: a model of similarity-based retrieval
finding: Two-stage retrieval: a cheap content-vector scan (MAC) returns a few candidates, then a structure-mapping match (FAC) picks the best. Covered by the parallel Analogical retrieval subfield; only linked here.
numbers: Not opened (fetch failed).
limits: Marked [M]. Overlaps another subfield.
agent_relevance: Two-stage design (cheap recall, then careful rerank) matches BM25 then learned reranker in EPR.

source: Liu et al. (2021) What makes good in-context examples for GPT-3? (KATE)
finding: Choosing the k nearest training examples to the test input as GPT-3 prompt examples beats random examples. GPT-3 is very sensitive to which examples are used: SST-2 with five random example sets scored 94.6, 95.0, 95.8, 93.9, 86.9.
numbers: Abstract: relative gains of 41.9% on ToTTo table-to-text and 45.5% on Natural Questions (EM) over random. Order test on NQ with KATE-nli+sts-b: 42.0, 42.5, 42.0 for 3 random orders, 41.6 default, 42.8 reverse (closest example last).
limits: GPT-3, 2021. Encoder matters: encoders fine-tuned on NLI or STS-B beat plain RoBERTa. One run per cell in several tables.
agent_relevance: First direct evidence that nearest-case retrieval beats random for an LLM. Order of retrieved cases moved results by about 1 point.

source: Liu et al. (2021) KATE: IMDB transfer and encoder tests
finding: Retrieval from a different domain still helps if the encoder is tuned. Three examples used.
numbers: IMDB accuracy with SST-2 examples: Random 87.95 +- 2.74; KATE-sst2 93.43; KATE-roberta 91.99; KATE-nli 90.40; KATE-nli+sts-b 90.20. A kNN row printed 50.20 (label unclear in the extracted text).
limits: Table text partly garbled in extraction; the 50.20 row not identified with certainty.
agent_relevance: A bad similarity function can be worse than random. Always include a random-case control.

source: Rubin, Herzig and Berant (2022) Learning to retrieve prompts for in-context learning (EPR)
finding: Train a dense retriever so examples that make the LM produce the right output are positives. Beats BM25, SBERT and a prior CBR-style retriever. Learned usefulness beats surface similarity.
numbers: GPT-Neo 2.7B, full dev sets, best baseline to EPR: BREAK 26.0 to 31.9; MTOP 57.0 to 64.2; SMCalFlow 51.4 to 54.3. Test: BREAK 23.9 vs BM25 17.6 vs CBR 18.4; MTOP 64.4 vs 49.0 vs 57.5. Random: 1.7, 7.3, 8.9.
limits: Three semantic parsing sets only. Needs labelled data and a scoring LM. LM-ORACLE (uses LM scores at test time) reaches 43.1 / 71.6 / 73.7, so a large gap remains.
agent_relevance: Retrieval is a learned choice, not a fixed similarity. Positives are defined by downstream success.

source: Rubin et al. (2022) EPR: BM25 versus SBERT and the BM25 oracle
finding: BM25 word overlap beat SBERT dense similarity for prompt retrieval on all three sets. EPR matched or beat an oracle that sees the gold output and picks BM25-nearest by output similarity.
numbers: Dev, GPT-Neo, BREAK/MTOP/SMCalFlow: SBERT 21.6/48.7/43.6; BM25 26.0/52.9/46.1; BM25-ORACLE 32.3/58.9/47.3; EPR 31.9/64.2/54.3. Brute-force 200-sample labelling retriever: 7.7/18.1/11.1.
limits: Semantic parsing, where output form matters more than topic. May not carry to free text.
agent_relevance: The best nearest case shares output structure with the problem, not topic. Topic-embedding similarity is a weak guide.

source: Ye et al. (2023) Compositional exemplars for in-context learning (CEIL)
finding: Select the set of examples jointly with a determinantal point process, so examples are relevant and not redundant. 12 datasets, 7 tasks, GPT-Neo 2.7B.
numbers: Average over 12 datasets: Random 30.68; TopK-BM25 45.84; TopK-Contriever 45.73; TopK-SimCSE 45.19; TopK-BERT 45.65; DPP-BERT 45.43; EPR 53.37; CEIL 56.76 (+3.39 over EPR). Largest gains over EPR: SMCalFlow +6.43, MNLI +5.68, QNLI +4.65. Row-to-label mapping inferred, consistent with EPR's own random and BM25 values.
limits: Generation tasks gained more than classification. CommonsenseQA and HellaSwag gains under 1 point. Extracted table labels were shifted by one row.
agent_relevance: Off-the-shelf encoders all landed within 0.7 points of each other, so swapping encoders buys little. Learning from LM feedback bought about 7.5 points; set-level selection 3.4 more. Diversity inside the retrieved set matters.

source: Su et al. (2022) Selective annotation makes language models better few-shot learners (vote-k)
finding: Which cases are stored matters as much as how they are retrieved. Picking diverse, representative cases (vote-k) then retrieving by similarity beats random annotation. Random retrieval does not benefit from the better pool.
numbers: 10 datasets. Relative gain over random annotation: 11.4% at budget 100 and 12.9% at budget 18 (absolute 5.2 and 5.8 points). Table 4, budget 100, vote-k with similar vs random retrieval: HellaSwag 70.7 vs 65.2, SST-5 53.0 vs 44.2, MWoZ 51.4 vs 35.6.
limits: GPT-J / GPT-Neo era. The random vs vote-k gap shrank with a larger model (HellaSwag 7.5% vs 2.6%).
agent_relevance: Retention and retrieval interact: a diverse library pays off only if retrieval is similarity-based.

source: Li et al. (2023) Unified demonstration retriever for in-context learning (UDR)
finding: One retriever trained across 30+ tasks in 13 families with list-wise ranking from LM feedback transfers to unseen datasets and to several LMs.
numbers: Unseen sets, UDR vs BM25 vs SBERT: Twitter 56.8 vs 50.0 vs 51.6; QNLI 74.4 vs 54.1 vs 53.7; Ruby 19.6 vs 9.2 vs 8.7; JavaScript 21.6 vs 12.7 vs 15.9. SMCalFlow, Text-Davinci-003: BM25 55.0, EPR 58.9, UDR 64.7. Ablation avg: UDR 58.4, no multitask 56.5, no rank loss 55.7.
limits: Summarisation sets showed little retriever effect (LM already knows the task).
agent_relevance: A retriever trained once on many tasks generalises, promising for a library that must serve new problems.

source: Wang, Yang and Wei (2023) Learning to retrieve in-context examples for large language models (LLM-R)
finding: Iteratively trained dense retriever from an LLM reward model. Improves over random by 7.8% on average over 30 tasks (abstract), also on held-out tasks and LMs of varying size.
numbers: Table 1 average column as extracted: SBERT 62.1, EPR 63.5, LLM-R 1 iteration 65.7, 2 iterations 66.5, 3 iterations 66.4. BM25 used to bootstrap candidates; E5 vs BM25 bootstrapping marginal.
limits: Extracted table alignment is uncertain, so only the ordering is relied on. Gains stop after 2 iterations.
agent_relevance: Retrieve-score-retrain converges in about two rounds.

source: Luo et al. (2023) Dr.ICL: demonstration-retrieved in-context learning
finding: Even simple BM25 word overlap beats random demonstrations for PaLM and for instruction-tuned Flan-PaLM, including with chain-of-thought prompts. Trained retrievers help more.
numbers: Only qualitative statements recorded; figure values were not extractable from the text version.
limits: No clean numbers captured, so no effect size is claimed.
agent_relevance: Nearest-case advantage extends to instruction-tuned models and reasoning prompts.

source: Min et al. (2022) Rethinking the role of demonstrations: what makes in-context learning work?
finding: Counter-finding that limits the retrieval story. Randomly replacing the labels of in-context examples barely hurts classification and multi-choice tasks, consistently across 12 models. What examples supply is the label space, the input distribution and the format.
numbers: 12 models including the GPT-3 family and MetaICL. Random-label drop described as marginal; exact per-model deltas not recorded.
quote: replacing the labels in demonstrations with random labels barely hurts performance
limits: Fixed random demonstrations, not retrieved near-duplicates. Where retrieved cases are close to the query, copying their label may matter, which this study did not test.
agent_relevance: Retrieval value may come from format and input match rather than the stored answers. Test whether the agent uses a case's answer or only its shape.

source: Lewis et al. (2020) Retrieval-augmented generation for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks (RAG)
finding: Dense nearest-neighbour retrieval over Wikipedia chunks (DPR, MIPS with FAISS) feeding a seq2seq generator, trained end to end. Learned dense retriever beats BM25 on most tasks.
numbers: Test EM, RAG-Sequence: NQ 44.5, TriviaQA 56.8 (68.0 on the open test), WebQ 45.2, CuratedTrec 52.2; DPR 41.5/57.9/41.1/50.6; T5-11B closed-book NQ 34.5. Dev ablation NQ: BM25 retriever 31.8, frozen retriever 41.2, learned 44.0. Correct answer produced 11.8% of the time on NQ when it is in no retrieved document.
limits: Fact retrieval, not case retrieval. BM25 was better on FEVER (entity-heavy).
agent_relevance: Learning the retriever with the generator gained about 12 EM over BM25 on NQ. Same lesson as EPR.

source: Das et al. (2021) Case-based reasoning for natural language queries over knowledge bases (CBR-KBQA)
finding: Neural CBR: retrieve similar questions by relational similarity of their logical forms (not shared entities), generate with a seq2seq reuse model, then align to the KB. New relations can be added as cases without retraining.
numbers: CWQ test accuracy 67.1 vs T5-11B 52.4 (+11 over previous best system). CFQ MCD mean 78.1 vs T5-11B 67.7. WebQSP accuracy by retrieved cases: K=0 67.20, K=1 68.45, K=10 69.23, K=20 69.98. Human-added cases lifted unseen-relation F1 from 0.0 to 36.39 with no retraining. Retriever recall of gold relations: RoBERTa untuned 86.6 to 90.4 tuned (WebQSP), 94.8 to 98.4 (CFQ).
limits: KBQA only. Gain from cases is small on WebQSP (+2.8 at K=20) but large on novel combinations.
agent_relevance: Retrieve for relational similarity, not entity overlap. This is the same as retrieving by problem class, not wording.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: fine-tuning LLM agents without fine-tuning LLMs
finding: Agent with a growing case bank of (state, plan, reward) retrieved by cosine similarity (non-parametric) or a learned Q-function (parametric). No weight updates. Case memory adds accuracy mainly out of distribution.
numbers: GAIA validation 87.88% Pass@3, test 79.40%. DeepResearcher F1 66.6, PM 80.4. Ablation CBR gain F1/PM: HLE +4.5/+7.0, SimpleQA +3.7/+5.3, DeepResearcher +6.7/+8.2. PM over 5 learning rounds on DeepResearcher at iteration 5: no CBR 84.47, non-parametric 84.85, parametric 85.44.
limits: Authors note data contamination in DeepResearcher; the no-planning step even lost 18.0 F1 on open-domain data. Planner GPT-4.1, executor o4-mini.
agent_relevance: Learned case selection beat plain cosine by only about 0.6 points after 5 rounds. Same shape as CASCADE.

source: Zhou et al. (2025) Memento: number of retrieved cases K
finding: Retrieved case count saturates fast. Four cases is about best; beyond that results are flat or worse.
limits: One planner and executor pair. Single run per cell.
agent_relevance: Most of the gain comes from the first one or two cases. Offer few cases, not many.

source: Guo et al. (2026) CASCADE: case-based continual adaptation for LLMs during deployment
finding: Case retrieval as a contextual bandit (Neural-LinLogUCB). Compared with plain similarity retrieval (NP-CBR). Adaptive retrieval adds a few points on top of similarity retrieval, which already gives most of the gain over zero-shot.
numbers: Qwen3-32B, 12 single-turn tasks: NP-CBR average success 63.76% to CASCADE 66.68%. Web search 53.29% to 66.51%; local RAG 45.94% to 50.06%. MIMIC-III: zero-shot 20.75%, NP-CBR 44.02%, CASCADE 55.76%. Headline +20.9% macro over zero-shot (metric definition not matched to the 12-task numbers). Beat REINFORCE+LoRA on 9 of 12 tasks with one case, the rest with four cases.
limits: Preprint, 5 seeds, binary feedback. Fails when the model never succeeds zero-shot (Qwen3-4B on MIMIC-IV-MR: all methods 0).
agent_relevance: Learning which case to retrieve from outcome is the right frame; similarity-only retrieval is a strong baseline. Needs a minimum base ability to produce any successes.

source: Huawei group (2025) Optimizing CBR system for functional test script generation (CBR+Re4)
finding: Retrieval of similar past test cases with bge-m3 gave about 15 points over fine-tuning alone on a 7B model; training for rewrite and rerank (Re4) added 2 to 4 more.
numbers: FF1 on DCN: naive SFT 49.46, naive CBR 64.01, CBR 64.67, CBR+SFT 67.87, CBR+Re4 70.11. SP: 38.71, 54.60, 55.83, 57.98, 61.92. Single run.
limits: Industrial data from two product units; internal 7B model; not public. Figures taken from the notes file and the paper start, not re-derived. Numbers copied from the project notes file; paper not re-read this session.
agent_relevance: Retrieval beat weight training by a large margin when similar cases exist.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the middle: how language models use long contexts
finding: Retrieved passages are not used equally. Accuracy is highest when the relevant passage is first or last in the prompt and lowest in the middle. More retrieved items do not mean more use.
numbers: 20-document multi-document QA, GPT-3.5-Turbo: accuracy falls by more than 20 points when the answer is in the middle, in the worst case below its closed-book score of 56.1%. Oracle (gold document only) 88.3%.
limits: 2023 models; newer long-context models may be less affected.
agent_relevance: Put the best retrieved case first or last and keep k small.

source: Wilkerson and Leake (cited in project notes) LLM retrieval versus k-NN
finding: Claim seen only in a search summary earlier in this project: asking an LLM to pick cases directly matched the k-NN choice only 20 to 28 percent of the time. Not relied on.
numbers: Not opened. Numbers unverified.
limits: Marked [M]; source not located this session (web search budget used up, API rate limits).
agent_relevance: If true, an LLM cannot be trusted to do its own case selection, which supports G5 (code selects).
